label: Single-pump vacuum hardware reference conversion

pump.facts: 0.6 kg; drawing envelope 106 x 43 x 74 mm; 6.5 L/min STP at atmosphere; 100 mbar absolute ultimate vacuum; 24 V and maximum 0.65 A.
pump.curve_basis: Coarse manual readings of the N86 KNDC vacuum-side plot on page 3; interpolated points are approximate, not manufacturer tabulated numerical data. The 100 and 1000 mbar endpoints use the specified endpoint ratings. The datasheet says STP without defining its temperature/pressure; this model explicitly assumes 273.15 K and 101325 Pa for conversion to ambient-volume leakage.

valves.facts: 2/2 normally closed vacuum-compatible valve; vacuum at connection 2; 10 g, 24 V DC, 1 W, opening 4 ms and closing 5 ms; 10 mm family width.
valves.geometry_basis: Conservative 42 x 10 x 28 mm collision envelope covering valve and connector; simplified assumed bounding box, not a CAD reproduction. Eight valves provide four isolation and four atmospheric vent paths.

hose.facts: OD 6 mm, ID 4 mm, 0.0183 kg/m; vacuum rating -0.95 bar; flow-relevant bending radius 26 mm.
hose.geometry_basis: Fixed straight collision segments and rigidly carried mass. Endpoints, route length and bends are installation assumptions. Tube flexibility, bend losses and fatigue are not simulated.

pump.inertia_basis: Uniform envelope box approximation. Manufacturer gives total mass and outside dimensions, not the internal COM or inertia tensor.
pump.position_basis: Assumed rear-top mount, bottom 188 mm above chassis frame origin; not a finished mechanical design.

mount_plate.basis: Assumed solid aluminium plate without holes. Mass is density times volume.

manifold.basis: Assumed custom manifold including fittings; outside envelope and mass allowance, not a sourced commercial part.

valves.basis: Sourced valve mass, rating and switching delay; assumed connector envelope and mounting positions.

hose.basis: Sourced tube dimensions and linear mass, assumed retained routing waypoints; each final point is derived from its real skirt backplate port. No rotating pneumatic interfaces, straight segments only, no flexural dynamics.

electrics.basis: Assumed driver, cable and connector allowance. Existing vehicle battery is retained; no new battery is silently assigned zero mass. Electrical compatibility and capacity remain unverified.

pneumatics.basis: One pump supplies a shared manifold and delayed isolation/vent valves. High conductance open branches are mixed by gas-volume conservation; no per-wheel copy of total pump flow. Per-branch chamber volume is derived from the real nominal skirt void plus its actual hose inner volume. Common volume is assumed manifold/pump void plus main-hose inner volume. Leak values and STP conversion conditions are explicit reduced-order assumptions. The 8 kPa operating cap is a relief/control assumption retained from the previous experiment, not the pump ultimate-vacuum rating.
pneumatics.regulation_basis: Assumed ideal average-duty regulator at the inherited 8 kPa operating cap. Pump dynamics and pressure ripple are not resolved; duty and one-pump average flow are reported.
pneumatics.energy_basis: Pump running power uses its 24 V x 0.65 A nameplate maximum times reported average duty as an upper-bound estimate, plus rated energized valve power. Not measured consumption; no total vehicle electrical power claim.

limitations: This is a source-attributed pump and valve installation envelope with rigid mass and collision, not manufacturing CAD or a validated bill of materials.
Valve/connector envelopes, all mounting positions, manifold mass and electronics allowance are assumptions. Default skirt shoes are fixed to the car and need no rotary pneumatic union.
Pump curve points are coarse manual estimates from a published graph; actual installed flow, seal leakage and electrical power require measurement.
Pneumatic branches share one pump. Mixing neglects finite branch pressure gradients and bend losses; contact loss opens leakage during physical valve switching delay.
Flexible hose deformation, rotating seal drag, vibration isolation, thermal loading and cable routing are not resolved.
The separate seal model owns four fixed underbody skirt shoes and their actual geometric area. This file does not make an ordinary J100 tire a suction cup.
